xml:id.name: xml:id
xml:id.doc: Regularizes the naming of an element and thus facilitates building links between it and other resources. Each id attribute within a document must have a unique value.

xml:base#2.name: xml:base
xml:base#2.doc: Provides a base URI reference with which applications can resolve relative URI references into absolute URI references.

label.name: label
label.doc: Captures text to be used to generate a label for the element to which it’s attached, a "tool tip" or prefatory text, for example. Should not be used to record document content.

copyof.name: copyof
copyof.doc: Points to an element of which the current element is a copy.

corresp.name: corresp
corresp.doc: Used to point to other elements that correspond to this one in a generic fashion.

follows.name: follows
follows.doc: points to one or more events in a user-defined collection that are known to be predecessors of the current element.

next.name: next
next.doc: Used to point to the next event(s) in a user-defined collection.

precedes.name: precedes
precedes.doc: Points to one or more events in a user-defined collection that are known to be successors of the current element.

prev.name: prev
prev.doc: Points to the previous event(s) in a user-defined collection.

sameas.name: sameas
sameas.doc: Points to an element that is the same as the current element but is not a literal copy of the current element.

synch.name: synch
synch.doc: Points to elements that are synchronous with the current element.

n.name: n
n.doc: Provides a number-like designation that indicates an element’s position in a sequence of similar elements. May not contain space characters.

resp.name: resp
resp.doc: Indicates the agent(s) responsible for some aspect of the text’s transcription, editing, or encoding. Its value must point to one or more identifiers declared in the document header.

class#2.name: class
class#2.doc: Contains one or more URIs which denote classification terms that apply to the entity bearing this attribute.

type#6.name: type
type#6.doc: Designation which characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology that employs single-token labels.

facs.name: facs
facs.doc: (facsimile) Points to one or more images, portions of an image, or surfaces which correspond to the current element.

when.name: when
when.doc: Indicates the point of occurrence of this feature along a time line. Its value must be the ID of a <when> element elsewhere in the document.

layer.name: layer
layer.doc: Identifies the layer to which a feature applies.

part.name: part
part.doc: Indicates the part in which the current feature should appear. Use '%all' when the feature should occur in every part.

partstaff.name: partstaff
partstaff.doc: Signifies the part staff on which a notated feature occurs. Use '%all' when the feature should occur on every staff.

plist.name: plist
plist.doc: When the target attribute is present, plist identifies the active participants; that is, those entities pointed "from", in a relationship with the specified target(s). When the target attribute is not present, it identifies participants in a mutual relationship.

staff.name: staff
staff.doc: Signifies the staff on which a notated event occurs or to which a control event applies. Mandatory when applicable.

evaluate.name: evaluate

values.doc: If an element pointed to is itself a pointer, then the target of that pointer will be taken, and so on, until an element is found which is not a pointer.
If an element pointed to is itself a pointer, then its target (whether a pointer or not) is taken as the target of this pointer.
No further evaluation of targets is carried out beyond that needed to find the element(s) specified in plist or target attribute.

evaluate.doc: Specifies the intended meaning when a participant in a relationship is itself a pointer.

tstamp.name: tstamp
tstamp.doc: (time stamp) Encodes the onset time in terms of musical time, i.e., beats[.fractional beat part], as expressed in the written time signature.

tstamp.ges.name: tstamp.ges
tstamp.ges.doc: Encodes the onset time in terms of musical time, i.e., beats[.fractional beat part], as expressed in the written time signature.

tstamp.real.name: tstamp.real
tstamp.real.doc: Records the onset time in terms of ISO time.

startid.name: startid
startid.doc: Holds a reference to the first element in a sequence of events to which the feature applies.

order#2.name: order

values.doc: Non-arpeggiated style (usually rendered with a preceding bracket instead of a wavy line).

order#2.doc: Describes the direction in which an arpeggio is to be performed.

altsym.name: altsym
altsym.doc: Provides a way of pointing to a user-defined symbol. It must contain a reference to an ID of a <symbolDef> element elsewhere in the document.

color#2.name: color
color#2.doc: Used to indicate visual appearance. Do not confuse this with the musical term 'color' as used in pre-CMN notation.

enclose.name: enclose
enclose.doc: Records the characters often used to mark accidentals, articulations, and sometimes notes as having a cautionary or editorial function. For an example of cautionary accidentals enclosed in parentheses, see Read, p. 131, ex. 9-14.

glyph.auth.name: glyph.auth
glyph.auth.doc: A name or label associated with the controlled vocabulary from which the value of @glyph.name or @glyph.num is taken, or the textual content of the element. Suggested values include: 1] smufl

glyph.uri.name: glyph.uri
glyph.uri.doc: The web-accessible location of the controlled vocabulary from which the value of @glyph.name or @glyph.num is taken, or the textual content of the element.

glyph.num.name: glyph.num
glyph.num.doc: Numeric glyph reference in hexadecimal notation, e.g., "#xE000" or "U+E000". N.B. SMuFL version 1.18 uses the range U+E000 - U+ECBF.

lform.name: lform
lform.doc: Describes the style of a line.

lsegs.name: lsegs
lsegs.doc: Describes the number of segments into which a dashed or dotted line may be divided, or the number of "peaks" of a wavy line; a pair of space-separated values (minimum and maximum, respectively) provides a range between which a rendering system-supplied value may fall, while a single value indicates a fixed amount of space; that is, the minimum and maximum values are equal.

fontfam.name: fontfam
fontfam.doc: Contains the name of a font-family.

fontname.name: fontname
fontname.doc: Holds the name of a font.

fontsize.name: fontsize

values.doc: Smaller than small, larger than xx-small.
Smaller than normal, larger than x-small.
Smaller than large, larger than small.
Smaller than x-large, larger than normal.
Smaller than xx-large, larger than large.
One size smaller than the current size.
One size larger than the current size.
Smaller than small, larger than xx-small.
Smaller than normal, larger than x-small.
Smaller than large, larger than small.
Smaller than x-large, larger than normal.
Smaller than xx-large, larger than large.
One size smaller than the current size.
One size larger than the current size.

fontsize.doc: Indicates the size of a font expressed in printers' points, i.e., 1/72nd of an inch, relative terms, e.g., small, larger, etc., or percentage values relative to normal size, e.g., 125%.

fontstyle.name: fontstyle
fontstyle.doc: Records the style of a font, i.e., italic, oblique, or normal.

letterspacing.name: letterspacing
letterspacing.doc: Indicates letter spacing (aka tracking) in analogy to the CSS letter-spacing property.

lineheight.name: lineheight
lineheight.doc: Indicates line height in analogy to the CSS line-height property.

ho.name: ho
ho.doc: Records a horizontal adjustment to a feature’s programmatically-determined location in terms of staff interline distance; that is, in units of 1/2 the distance between adjacent staff lines.

to#2.name: to
to#2.doc: Records a timestamp adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined location in terms of musical time; that is, beats.

vo.name: vo
vo.doc: Records the vertical adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined location in terms of staff interline distance; that is, in units of 1/2 the distance between adjacent staff lines.

x#4.name: x
x#4.doc: Encodes an x coordinate for a feature in an output coordinate system. When it is necessary to record the placement of a feature in a facsimile image, use the facs attribute.

y#4.name: y
y#4.doc: Encodes a y coordinate for a feature in an output coordinate system. When it is necessary to record the placement of a feature in a facsimile image, use the facs attribute.

arrow.name: arrow
arrow.doc: Indicates if an arrowhead is to be drawn as part of the arpeggiation symbol.

arrow.shape.name: arrow.shape

values.doc: 90 degree turn down (similar to Unicode 231D at end of line, 231C at start).
90 degree turn up (similar to Unicode 231F at end of line, 231E at start).
90 degree turn right (syntactic sugar for "angledown" for vertical or angled lines).
90 degree turn left (syntactic sugar for "angleup" for vertical or angled lines).
Filled, triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+25C0 or SMuFL U+EB78).
Open triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+02C3 or SMuFL U+EB8A).
Unfilled, triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+25C1 or SMuFL U+EB82).
Harpoon-shaped arrowhead left of line (similar to arrowhead of Unicode U+21BD).
Harpoon-shaped arrowhead right of line (similar to arrowhead of Unicode U+21BC).

arrow.shape.doc: Symbol rendered at end of the line.

arrow.size.name: arrow.size
arrow.size.doc: Holds the relative size of the arrow symbol.

arrow.color.name: arrow.color
arrow.color.doc: Captures the overall color of the arrow.

arrow.fillcolor.name: arrow.fillcolor
arrow.fillcolor.doc: Captures the fill color of the arrow if different from the line color.

xml:lang#2.name: xml:lang
xml:lang#2.doc: Identifies the language of the element’s content. The values for this attribute are language 'tags' as defined in BCP 47. All language tags that make use of private use sub-tags must be documented in a corresponding language element in the MEI header whose id attribute is the same as the language tag’s value.

endid.name: endid
endid.doc: Indicates the final element in a sequence of events to which the feature applies.

tstamp2.name: tstamp2
tstamp2.doc: Encodes the ending point of an event, i.e., a count of measures plus a beat location in the ending measure.

target#2.name: target
target#2.doc: Indicates the next section or movement to be performed.

lendsym.name: lendsym

values.doc: 90 degree turn down (similar to Unicode 231D at end of line, 231C at start).
90 degree turn up (similar to Unicode 231F at end of line, 231E at start).
90 degree turn right (syntactic sugar for "angledown" for vertical or angled lines).
90 degree turn left (syntactic sugar for "angleup" for vertical or angled lines).
Filled, triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+25C0 or SMuFL U+EB78).
Open triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+02C3 or SMuFL U+EB8A).
Unfilled, triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+25C1 or SMuFL U+EB82).
Harpoon-shaped arrowhead left of line (similar to arrowhead of Unicode U+21BD).
Harpoon-shaped arrowhead right of line (similar to arrowhead of Unicode U+21BC).

lendsym.doc: (line end symbol) Symbol rendered at end of line.

lendsym.size.name: lendsym.size
lendsym.size.doc: Holds the relative size of the line-end symbol.

lstartsym.name: lstartsym

values.doc: 90 degree turn down (similar to Unicode 231D at end of line, 231C at start).
90 degree turn up (similar to Unicode 231F at end of line, 231E at start).
90 degree turn right (syntactic sugar for "angledown" for vertical or angled lines).
90 degree turn left (syntactic sugar for "angleup" for vertical or angled lines).
Filled, triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+25C0 or SMuFL U+EB78).
Open triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+02C3 or SMuFL U+EB8A).
Unfilled, triangular arrowhead (similar to Unicode U+25C1 or SMuFL U+EB82).
Harpoon-shaped arrowhead left of line (similar to arrowhead of Unicode U+21BD).
Harpoon-shaped arrowhead right of line (similar to arrowhead of Unicode U+21BC).

lstartsym.doc: (line start symbol) Symbol rendered at start of line.

lstartsym.size.name: lstartsym.size
lstartsym.size.doc: Holds the relative size of the line-start symbol.

extender.name: extender
extender.doc: Indicates the presence of an extension symbol, typically a line.

place.name: place
place.doc: Captures the placement of the item with respect to the staff with which it is associated.

vgrp.name: vgrp
vgrp.doc: Provides a label for members of a vertically aligned group.

startho.name: startho
startho.doc: Records the horizontal adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined start point.

endho.name: endho
endho.doc: Records the horizontal adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined end point.

startto.name: startto
startto.doc: Records a timestamp adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined start point.

endto.name: endto
endto.doc: Records a timestamp adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined end point.

tstamp2.ges.name: tstamp2.ges
tstamp2.ges.doc: Encodes the ending point of an event, i.e., a count of measures plus a beat location in the ending measure.

tstamp2.real.name: tstamp2.real
tstamp2.real.doc: Records the ending point of an event in terms of ISO time.

beam.with.name: beam.with
beam.with.doc: In the case of cross-staff beams, the beam.with attribute is used to indicate which staff the beam is connected to; that is, the staff above or the staff below.

form.name: form

values.doc: (accelerando) means that the secondary beams become progressively more distant toward the end of the beam.
(mixed acc and rit) for beams that are "feathered" in both directions.
(ritardando) indicates that the secondary beams get progressively closer together toward the end of the beam.
(normal) indicates that the secondary beams are equidistant along the course of the beam.

form.doc: Captures whether a beam is "feathered" and in which direction.

place#2.name: place

values.doc: The beam is above the events it affects.
The beam is below the events it affects.
The beam is above and below the events it affects.

place#2.doc: Records the placement of the beam relative to the events it affects.

slash.name: slash
slash.doc: Indicates presence of slash through the beam.

slope#2.name: slope
slope#2.doc: Records the slope of the beam.

visible.name: visible
visible.doc: Indicates if a feature should be rendered when the notation is presented graphically or sounded when it is presented in an aural form.

dots.ges.name: dots.ges
dots.ges.doc: Number of dots required for a gestural duration when different from that of the written duration.

dur.metrical.name: dur.metrical
dur.metrical.doc: Duration as a count of units provided in the time signature denominator.

dur.ppq.name: dur.ppq
dur.ppq.doc: Duration recorded as pulses-per-quarter note, e.g., MIDI clicks or MusicXML divisions.

dur.recip.name: dur.recip
dur.recip.doc: Duration as an optionally dotted Humdrum **recip value.

beatdef.name: beatdef
beatdef.doc: Indicates the performed duration represented by the beatRpt symbol; expressed in time signature denominator units.

expand.name: expand
expand.doc: Indicates whether to render a repeat symbol or the source material to which it refers. A value of 'true' renders the source material, while 'false' displays the repeat symbol.

slash#2.name: slash
slash#2.doc: Indicates the number of slashes required to render the appropriate beat repeat symbol. When a single beat consisting of a single note or chord is repeated, the repetition symbol is a single thick, slanting slash; therefore, the value 1 should be used. When the beat is divided into even notes, the following values should be used: 4ths or 8ths=1, 16ths=2, 32nds=3, 64ths=4, 128ths=5. When the beat is comprised of mixed duration values, the default rendition is 2 slashes and 2 dots.

bezier.name: bezier
bezier.doc: Records the placement of Bezier control points as a series of pairs of space-separated values; e.g., 19 45 -32 118.

bulge.name: bulge
bulge.doc: Describes a curve as one or more pairs of values with respect to an imaginary line connecting the starting and ending points of the curve. The first value captures a distance to the left (positive value) or right (negative value) of the line, expressed in virtual units. The second value of each pair represents a point along the line, expressed as a percentage of the line’s length. N.B. An MEI virtual unit (vu) is half the distance between adjacent staff lines where the interline space is measured from the middle of a staff line.

curvedir.name: curvedir

values.doc: A "meandering" curve, both above and below the items it pertains to.

curvedir.doc: Describes a curve with a generic term indicating the direction of curvature.

startvo.name: startvo
startvo.doc: Records a vertical adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined start point.

endvo.name: endvo
endvo.doc: Records a vertical adjustment of a feature’s programmatically-determined end point.

amount.name: amount
amount.doc: Records the amount of detuning. The decimal values should be rendered as a fraction (or an integer plus a fraction) along with the bend symbol.

func.name: func

values.doc: Represents coloration in the mensural notation source material.
Marks a sequence which does not match the current meter.
Represents a ligature in the mensural notation source material.
Represents coloration in the mensural notation source material.
Marks a sequence which does not match the current meter.
Represents a ligature in the mensural notation source material.

func.doc: (function) Describes the function of the bracketed event sequence. Suggested values include: 1] coloration; 2] cross-rhythm; 3] ligature

loc.name: loc
loc.doc: Holds the staff location of the feature.

ploc.name: ploc
ploc.doc: Captures staff location in terms of written pitch name.

oloc.name: oloc
oloc.doc: Records staff location in terms of written octave.

dots.name: dots
dots.doc: Records the number of augmentation dots required by a written dotted duration.

num.name: num
num.doc: (number) Records a number or count accompanying a notational feature.

form#2.name: form
form#2.doc: Describes the style of the tremolo.

num.place.name: num.place
num.place.doc: (number placement) States where the tuplet number will be placed in relation to the note heads.

num.visible.name: num.visible
num.visible.doc: Determines if the tuplet number is visible.

unitdur.name: unitdur
unitdur.doc: The performed duration of an individual note in a measured tremolo.

form#3.name: form

values.doc: Inverted, i.e., curve or bracket below the dot.
Upright; i.e., curve or bracket above the dot.

form#3.doc: Describes the visual appearance of the fermata; that is, whether it occurs as upright or inverted.

shape.name: shape

values.doc: A curve above or below the dot.
A bracket above or below the dot.
A triangle above or below the dot.

shape.doc: Describes the visual appearance of the fermata; that is, whether it has a curved, square, or angular shape.

beams.name: beams
beams.doc: Indicates the number of beams present.

beams.float.name: beams.float
beams.float.doc: Captures the number of "floating" beams, i.e., those not attached to stems.

float.gap.name: float.gap
float.gap.doc: Records the amount of separation between floating beams and stems.

grace.name: grace

values.doc: No interpretation regarding performed value of grace note.

grace.doc: Marks a note or chord as a "grace" (without a definite performed duration) and records from which other note/chord it should "steal" time.

grace.time.name: grace.time
grace.time.doc: Records the amount of time to be "stolen" from a non-grace note/chord.

attach.name: attach
attach.doc: Records whether the grace note group is attached to the following event or to the preceding one. The usual name for the latter is "Nachschlag".

form#4.name: form
form#4.doc: Captures the visual rendition and function of the hairpin; that is, whether it indicates an increase or a decrease in volume.

niente.name: niente
niente.doc: Indicates that the hairpin starts from or ends in silence. Often rendered as a small circle attached to the closed end of the hairpin. See Gould, p. 108.

opening.name: opening
opening.doc: Specifies the distance between the lines at the open end of a hairpin dynamic mark.

closed.name: closed
closed.doc: Applies to a "Rossini" hairpin, i.e., one where the normally open side is closed by a connecting line.

opening.vertical.name: opening.vertical
opening.vertical.doc: Indicates that the opening points are aligned with an imaginary line that is always 90° perpendicular to the horizontal plane, regardless of any angle or start/end adjustments, including when the hairpin is angled with @angle.optimize or through @endvo/@startvo adjustments.

angle.optimize.name: angle.optimize
angle.optimize.doc: Indicates that the slope of the hairpin can be adjusted to follow the content in order to optimize spacing.

c.name: c
c.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s C strings.

d#2.name: d
d#2.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s D strings.

e.name: e
e.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s E strings.

f.name: f
f.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s F strings.

g.name: g
g.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s G strings.

a.name: a
a.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s A strings.

b.name: b
b.doc: Indicates the pedal setting for the harp’s B strings.

decls.name: decls
decls.doc: Identifies one or more metadata elements (other than classification terms) within the header, which are understood to apply to the element bearing this attribute and its content.

xlink:actuate#3.name: xlink:actuate

values.doc: Load the target resource(s) upon user request.
Do not permit loading of the target resource(s).
Behavior other than allowed by the other values of this attribute.

xlink:actuate#3.doc: Defines whether a link occurs automatically or must be requested by the user.

xlink:role#2.name: xlink:role
xlink:role#2.doc: Characterization of the relationship between resources. The value of the role attribute must be a URI.

xlink:show#4.name: xlink:show

values.doc: Load the referenced resource in the same window.
Embed the referenced resource at the point of the link.
Do not permit traversal to the referenced resource.
Behavior other than permitted by the other values of this attribute.

xlink:show#4.doc: Defines how a remote resource is rendered.

target#3.name: target
target#3.doc: Identifies passive participants in a relationship; that is, the entities pointed "to".

targettype.name: targettype
targettype.doc: Characterization of target resource(s) using any convenient classification scheme or typology.

join.name: join
join.doc: Used for linking visually separate entities that form a single logical entity, for example, multiple slurs broken across a system break that form a single musical phrase. Also used to indicate a measure which metrically completes the current one. Record the identifiers of the separately encoded components, excluding the one carrying the attribute.

metcon.name: metcon
metcon.doc: (meter conformance) Indicates the relationship between the content of a measure and the prevailing meter.

control.name: control
control.doc: Indicates whether or not a bar line is "controlling"; that is, if it indicates a point of alignment across all the parts. Bar lines within a score are usually controlling; that is, they "line up". Bar lines within parts may or may not be controlling. When applied to <measure>, this attribute indicates the nature of the right bar line but not the left.

left.name: left

values.doc: Double bar line (SMuFL E031 and Unicode 1D101).
Segno serpent with vertical lines (SMuFL E04B).
End bar line (SMuFL E032 and Unicode 1D102).
Single bar line (SMuFL E030 and Unicode 1D100).

left.doc: Indicates the visual rendition of the left bar line. It is present here only for facilitation of translation from legacy encodings which use it. Usually, it can be safely ignored.

right.name: right

values.doc: Double bar line (SMuFL E031 and Unicode 1D101).
Segno serpent with vertical lines (SMuFL E04B).
End bar line (SMuFL E032 and Unicode 1D102).
Single bar line (SMuFL E030 and Unicode 1D100).

right.doc: Indicates the function of the right bar line and is structurally important.

bar.len.name: bar.len
bar.len.doc: States the length of bar lines in virtual units. The value must be greater than 0 and is typically equal to 2 times (the number of staff lines - 1); e.g., a value of 8 for a 5-line staff.

values.doc: Between and across staves as necessary.
Short bar line through a subset of staff lines.

bar.place.name: bar.place
bar.place.doc: Denotes the staff location of bar lines, if the length is non-standard; that is, not equal to 2 times (the number of staff lines - 1).

width#2.name: width
width#2.doc: Measurement of the horizontal dimension of an entity.

count.name: count
count.doc: Captures the number of beats in a measure, that is, the top number of the meter signature. It must contain a decimal number or an expression that evaluates to a decimal number, such as 2+3 or 3*2.

sym.name: sym

values.doc: Open time signature, i.e., Senza misura. See Gould pp. 611–615.

sym.doc: (symbol) Indicates the use of a meter symbol instead of a numeric meter signature, that is, 'C' for common time or 'C' with a slash for cut time.

unit.name: unit
unit.doc: Contains the number indicating the beat unit, that is, the bottom number of the meter signature.

form#5.name: form

values.doc: Show only the number of beats.
The lower number in the meter signature is replaced by a note symbol.
Meter signature rendered using traditional numeric values.
Meter signature rendered using both the symbol and the traditional numeric values.

form#5.doc: Contains an indication of how the meter signature should be rendered.

func#2.name: func

values.doc: A registered Unicode normative or informative property name.

arpeg.doc: (arpeggiation) Indicates that the notes of a chord are to be performed successively rather than simultaneously, usually from lowest to highest. Sometimes called a "roll".

attacca.doc: An instruction to begin the next section or movement of a composition without pause.

beam.doc: A container for a series of explicitly beamed events that begins and ends entirely within a measure.

beamSpan.doc: (beam span) Alternative element for explicitly encoding beams, particularly those which extend across bar lines.

beatRpt.doc: (beat repeat) An indication that material on a preceding beat should be repeated.

bend.doc: A variation in pitch (often micro-tonal) upwards or downwards during the course of a note.

bracketSpan.doc: Marks a sequence of notational events grouped by a bracket.

breath.doc: (breath mark) An indication of a point at which the performer on an instrument requiring breath (including the voice) may breathe.

bTrem.doc: (bowed tremolo) A rapid alternation on a single pitch or chord.

fermata.doc: An indication placed over a note or rest to indicate that it should be held longer than its written value. May also occur over a bar line to indicate the end of a phrase or section. Sometimes called a 'hold' or 'pause'.

fTrem.doc: (fingered tremolo) A rapid alternation between a pair of notes (or chords or perhaps between a note and a chord) that are (usually) farther apart than a major second.

gliss.doc: (glissando) A continuous or sliding movement from one pitch to another, usually indicated by a straight or wavy line.

graceGrp.doc: (grace group) A container for a sequence of grace notes.

hairpin.doc: Indicates continuous dynamics expressed on the score as wedge-shaped graphics, e.g., < and >.

halfmRpt.doc: (half-measure repeat) A half-measure repeat in any meter.

lv.doc: (laissez vibrer) A "tie-like" indication that a note should ring beyond its written duration.

measure.doc: Unit of musical time consisting of a fixed number of note values of a given type, as determined by the prevailing meter, and delimited in musical notation by bar lines.

meterSigGrp.doc: (meter signature group) Used to capture alternating, interchanging, mixed or other non-standard meter signatures.

mNum.doc: (measure number) Designation, name, or label for a measure, often but not always consisting of digits. Use this element when the @n attribute on <measure> does not adequately capture the appearance or placement of the measure number/label.

mRest.doc: (measure rest) Complete measure rest in any meter.

mRpt.doc: (measure repeat) An indication that the previous measure should be repeated.

mRpt2.doc: (2-measure repeat) An indication that the previous two measures should be repeated.

mSpace.doc: (measure space) A measure containing only empty space in any meter.

multiRest.doc: (multiple rest) Multiple measures of rest compressed into a single symbol, frequently found in performer parts.

octave.doc: An indication that a passage should be performed one or more octaves above or below its written pitch.

oLayer.doc: (ossia layer) A layer that contains an alternative to material in another layer.

ossia.doc: Captures original notation and a differently notated version *present in the source being transcribed*.

oStaff.doc: (ossia staff) A staff that holds an alternative passage which may be played instead of the original material.

reh.doc: (rehearsal mark) In an orchestral score and its corresponding parts, a mark indicating a convenient point from which to resume rehearsal after a break.

repeatMark.doc: (repetition mark) An instruction expressed as a combination of text and symbols – segno and coda – typically above, below, or between staves, but not on the staff.

slur.doc: Indication of 1) a "unified melodic idea" or 2) performance technique.

tie.doc: An indication that two notes of the same pitch form a single note with their combined rhythmic values.

tuplet.doc: A group of notes with "irregular" (sometimes called "irrational") rhythmic values, for example, three notes in the time normally occupied by two or nine in the time of five.

tupletSpan.doc: (tuplet span) Alternative element for encoding tuplets, especially useful for tuplets that extend across bar lines.

mordent.doc: An ornament indicating rapid alternation of the main note with a secondary note, usually a step below, but sometimes a step above.

trill.doc: Rapid alternation of a note with another (usually at the interval of a second above).

turn.doc: An ornament consisting of four notes — the upper neighbor of the written note, the written note, the lower neighbor, and the written note.

meiCorpus.doc: (MEI corpus) A group of related MEI documents, consisting of a header for the group, and one or more <mei> elements, each with its own complete header.

app.doc: (apparatus) Contains one or more alternative encodings.

lem.doc: (lemma) Contains the lemma, or base text, of a textual variation.

rdg.doc: (reading) Contains a single reading within a textual variation.

sp.doc: (speech) Contains an individual speech in a performance text.

stageDir.doc: (stage direction) Contains any kind of stage direction within a dramatic text or fragment.

abbr.doc: (abbreviation) A generic element for 1) a shortened form of a word, including an acronym or 2) a shorthand notation.

add.doc: (addition) Marks an addition to the text.

choice.doc: Groups a number of alternative encodings for the same point in a text.

corr.doc: (correction) Contains the correct form of an apparent erroneous passage.

cpMark.doc: (copy/colla parte mark) A verbal or graphical indication to copy musical material written elsewhere.

damage.doc: Contains an area of damage to the physical medium.

del.doc: (deletion) Contains information deleted, marked as deleted, or otherwise indicated as superfluous or spurious in the copy text by an author, scribe, annotator, or corrector.

expan.doc: (expansion) Contains the expansion of an abbreviation.

gap.doc: Indicates a point where material has been omitted in a transcription, whether as part of sampling practice or for editorial reasons described in the MEI header.

handShift.doc: Marks the beginning of a passage written in a new hand, or of a change in the scribe, writing style, ink or character of the document hand.

metaMark.doc: A graphical or textual statement with additional / explanatory information about the musical text. The textual consequences of this intervention are encoded independently via other means; that is, with elements such as <add>, <del>, etc.

orig.doc: (original) Contains material which is marked as following the original, rather than being normalized or corrected.

reg.doc: (regularization) Contains material which has been regularized or normalized in some sense.

restore.doc: Indicates restoration of material to an earlier state by cancellation of an editorial or authorial marking or instruction.

sic.doc: Contains apparently incorrect or inaccurate material.

subst.doc: (substitution) Groups transcriptional elements when the combination is to be regarded as a single intervention in the text.

supplied.doc: Contains material supplied by the transcriber or editor for any reason.

unclear.doc: Contains material that cannot be transcribed with certainty because it is illegible or inaudible in the source.

facsimile.doc: Contains a representation of a written source in the form of a set of images rather than as transcribed or encoded text.

surface.doc: Defines a writing surface in terms of a rectangular coordinate space, optionally grouping one or more graphic representations of that space, and rectangular zones of interest within it.

zone.doc: Defines an area of interest within a <surface> or graphic file.

fig.doc: (figure) Groups elements representing or containing graphic information such as an illustration or figure.

figDesc.doc: (figure description) Contains a brief prose description of the appearance or content of a graphic figure, for use when documenting an image without displaying it.

graphic.doc: Indicates the location of an inline graphic.

table.doc: Contains text displayed in tabular form.

td.doc: (table data) Designates a table cell that contains data as opposed to a cell that contains column or row heading information.

th.doc: (table header) Designates a table cell containing column or row heading information as opposed to one containing data.

tr.doc: (table row) A formatting element that contains one or more cells (intersection of a row and a column) in a <table>.

fing.doc: (finger) An individual finger in a fingering indication.

fingGrp.doc: (finger group) A group of individual fingers in a fingering indication.

expression.doc: Intellectual or artistic realization of a work.

item.doc: Single instance or exemplar of a source/manifestation.

manifestation.doc: A bibliographic description of a physical embodiment of an expression of a work.

manifestationList.doc: A container for the descriptions of physical embodiments of an expression of a work.

genDesc.doc: (genetic description) Bundles information about the textual development of a work.

genState.doc: Describes a distinctive state in the textual development of a work.

chordMember.doc: An individual pitch in a chord defined by a <chordDef> element.

f.doc: (figure) Single element of a figured bass indication.

fb.doc: (figured bass) Symbols added to a bass line that indicate harmony. Used to improvise a chordal accompaniment. Sometimes called Generalbass, thoroughbass, or basso continuo.

harm.doc: (harmony) An indication of harmony, e.g., chord names, tablature grids, harmonic analysis, figured bass.

accessRestrict.doc: (access restriction) Describes the conditions that affect the accessibility of material.

acquisition.doc: Records information concerning the process by which an item was acquired by the holding institution.

altId.doc: (alternative identifier) May contain a bibliographic identifier that does not fit within the meiHead element’s id attribute, for example because the identifier does not fit the definition of an XML id or because multiple identifiers are needed.

appInfo.doc: (application information) Groups information about applications which have acted upon the MEI file.

application.doc: Provides information about an application which has acted upon the current document.

attUsage.doc: Documents the usage of a specific attribute of the element.

audience.doc: Defines the class of user for which the work is intended, as defined by age group (e.g., children, young adults, adults, etc.), educational level (e.g., primary, secondary, etc.), or other categorization.

availability.doc: Groups elements that describe the availability of and access to a bibliographic item, including an MEI-encoded document.

bifolium.doc: Describes a folded sheet of paper.

byline.doc: Contains the primary statement of responsibility given for a work on its title page.

captureMode.doc: (capture mode) The means used to record notation, sound, or images in the production of a source/manifestation (e.g., analogue, acoustic, electric, digital, optical etc.).

carrierForm.doc: (carrier form) The specific class of material to which the physical carrier of the source/manifestation belongs (e.g., sound cassette, videodisc, microfilm cartridge, transparency, etc.). The carrier for a manifestation comprising multiple physical components may include more than one form (e.g., a filmstrip with an accompanying booklet, a separate sound disc carrying the sound track for a film, etc.).

category.doc: Contains an individual descriptive category in a user-defined taxonomy, possibly nested within a superordinate category.

catRel.doc: (category relationship) Contains the name of a related category.

change.doc: Individual change within the revision description.

changeDesc.doc: (change description) Description of a revision of the MEI file.

classDecls.doc: Groups information which describes the nature or topic of an entity.

classification.doc: Groups information which describes the nature or topic of an entity.

componentList.doc: Container for intellectual or physical component parts of a bibliographic entity.

condition.doc: The physical condition of an item, particularly any variances between the physical make-up of the item and that of other copies of the same item (e.g., missing pages or plates, brittleness, faded images, etc.).

contentItem.doc: Contains a single entry within a content description element.

contents.doc: List of the material contained within a resource.

context.doc: The historical, social, intellectual, artistic, or other context within which the work was originally conceived (e.g., the 17th century restoration of the monarchy in England, the aesthetic movement of the late 19th century, etc.) or the historical, social, intellectual, artistic, or other context within which the expression was realized.

correction.doc: States how and under what circumstances corrections have been made in the text.

cutout.doc: A cutout is a section of a document sheet that has been removed and is now missing.

domainsDecl.doc: (domains declaration) Indicates which domains are included in the encoding.

editionStmt.doc: (edition statement) Container for meta-data pertaining to a particular edition of the material being described.

editorialDecl.doc: (editorial declaration) Used to provide details of editorial principles and practices applied during the encoding of musical text.

encodingDesc.doc: (encoding description) Documents the relationship between an electronic file and the source or sources from which it was derived as well as applications used in the encoding/editing process.

exhibHist.doc: (exhibition history) A record of public exhibitions, including dates, venues, etc.

extMeta.doc: (extended metadata) Provides a container element for non-MEI metadata formats.

fileChar.doc: (file characteristics) Standards or schemes used to encode the file (e.g., ASCII, SGML, etc.), physical characteristics of the file (e.g., recording density, parity, blocking, etc.), and other characteristics that have a bearing on how the file can be processed.

fileDesc.doc: (file description) Contains a full bibliographic description of the MEI file.

foliaDesc.doc: Describes the order of folia and bifolia making up the text block of a manuscript or print.

folium.doc: Describes a single leaf of paper.

hand.doc: Defines a distinct scribe or handwriting style.

handList.doc: Container for one or more hand elements.

history.doc: Provides a container for information about the history of a resource other than the circumstances of its creation.

incipCode.doc: Incipit coded in a non-XML, plain text format, such as Plaine & Easie Code.

incipText.doc: Opening words of a musical composition.

inscription.doc: An inscription added to an item, such as a bookplate, a note designating the item as a gift, and/or the author’s signature.

interpretation.doc: Describes the scope of any analytic or interpretive information added to the transcription of the music.

key.doc: Key captures information about tonal center and mode.

language.doc: Description of a language used in the document.

langUsage.doc: (language usage) Groups elements describing the languages, sub-languages, dialects, etc., represented within the encoded resource.

meiHead.doc: (MEI header) Supplies the descriptive and declarative metadata prefixed to every MEI-conformant text.

mensuration.doc: Captures information about mensuration within bibliographic descriptions.

meter.doc: Captures information about the time signature within bibliographic descriptions.

namespace.doc: Supplies the formal name of the namespace to which the elements documented by its children belong.

normalization.doc: Indicates the extent of normalization or regularization of the original source carried out in converting it to electronic form.

notesStmt.doc: (notes statement) Collects any notes providing information about a text additional to that recorded in other parts of the bibliographic description.

otherChar.doc: (other distinguishing characteristic) Any characteristic that serves to differentiate a work or expression from another.

patch.doc: Describes a physical writing surface attached to the original document.

perfDuration.doc: (performance duration) Used to express the duration of performance of printed or manuscript music or the playing time for a sound recording, videorecording, etc.

perfMedium.doc: (performance medium) Indicates the number and character of the performing forces used in a musical composition.

perfRes.doc: (performance resource) Name of an instrument on which a performer plays, a performer's voice range, or a standard performing ensemble designation.

perfResList.doc: (performance resources list) Several instrumental or vocal resources treated as a group.

physDesc.doc: (physical description) Container for information about the appearance, construction, or handling of physical materials, such as their dimension, quantity, color, style, and technique of creation.

physMedium.doc: (physical medium) Records the physical materials used in the source, such as ink and paper.

plateNum.doc: (plate number) Designation assigned to a resource by a music publisher, usually printed at the bottom of each page, and sometimes appearing also on the title page.

playingSpeed.doc: Playing speed for a sound recording is the speed at which the carrier must be operated to produce the sound intended (e.g., 33 1/3 rpm, 19 cm/s, etc.).

price.doc: The cost of access to a bibliographic item.

projectDesc.doc: (project description) Project-level meta-data describing the aim or purpose for which the electronic file was encoded, funding agencies, etc. together with any other relevant information concerning the process by which it was assembled or collected.

provenance.doc: The record of ownership or custodianship of an item.

pubStmt.doc: (publication statement) Container for information regarding the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item, including the publisher’s name and address, the date of publication, and other relevant details.

revisionDesc.doc: (revision description) Container for information about alterations that have been made to an MEI file.

samplingDecl.doc: (sampling declaration) Contains a prose description of the rationale and methods used in sampling texts in the creation of a corpus or collection.

scoreFormat.doc: Describes the type of score used to represent a musical composition (e.g., short score, full score, condensed score, close score, etc.).

segmentation.doc: Describes the principles according to which the musical text has been segmented, for example into movements, sections, etc.

seriesStmt.doc: (series statement) Groups information about the series, if any, to which a publication belongs.

soundChan.doc: (sound channels) Reflects the number of apparent sound channels in the playback of a recording (monaural, stereophonic, quadraphonic, etc.).

source.doc: A bibliographic description of a source used in the creation of the electronic file.

sourceDesc.doc: (source description) A container for the descriptions of the source(s) used in the creation of the electronic file.

specRepro.doc: (special reproduction characteristic) The equalization system, noise reduction system, etc. used in making the recording (e.g., NAB, DBX, Dolby, etc.).

stdVals.doc: (standard values) Specifies the format used when standardized date or number values are supplied.

sysReq.doc: (system requirements) System requirements for using the electronic item.

tagsDecl.doc: (tagging declaration) Provides detailed information about the tagging applied to a document.

tagUsage.doc: Documents the usage of a specific element within the document.

taxonomy.doc: Defines a typology either implicitly, by means of a bibliographic citation, or explicitly by a structured taxonomy.

termList.doc: Collection of text phrases which describe a resource.

titleStmt.doc: (title statement) Container for title and responsibility meta-data.

trackConfig.doc: (track configuration) Number of physical/input tracks on a sound medium (e.g., eight track, twelve track).

treatHist.doc: (treatment history) A record of the treatment the item has undergone (e.g., de-acidification, restoration, etc.).

treatSched.doc: (treatment scheduled) Scheduled treatment, e.g., de-acidification, restoration, etc., for an item.

unpub.doc: (unpublished) Used to explicitly indicate that a bibliographic resource is unpublished.

useRestrict.doc: (usage restrictions) Container for information about the conditions that affect use of a bibliographic item after access has been granted.

watermark.doc: Contains a description of a watermark or similar device.

work.doc: Provides a detailed description of a work — a distinct intellectual or artistic creation — specifically its history, language use, and high-level musical attributes (e.g., key, tempo, meter, medium of performance, and intended duration).

workList.doc: (work list) Grouping mechanism for information describing non-bibliographic aspects of a text.

refrain.doc: Recurring lyrics, especially at the end of each verse or stanza of a poem or song lyrics; a chorus.

verse.doc: Division of a poem or song lyrics, sometimes having a fixed length, meter or rhyme scheme; a stanza.

volta.doc: Sung text for a specific iteration of a repeated section of music.

ligature.doc: A mensural notation symbol that combines two or more notes into a single sign.

mensur.doc: (mensuration) Collects information about the metrical relationship between a note value and the next smaller value; that is, either triple or duple.

proport.doc: (proportion) Description of note duration as arithmetic ratio.

hex.doc: Arbitrary MIDI data in hexadecimal form.

midi.doc: Container for elements that contain information useful when generating MIDI output.

accMat.doc: Holds a description of any additional material bound with an item, such as non-contemporaneous documents or fragments.

addDesc.doc: (addition description) Provides a description of significant additions found within an item, such as marginalia or other annotations.

binding.doc: (binding) Contains a description of one binding, i.e., type of covering, boards, etc. applied to an item.

bindingDesc.doc: (binding description) Describes the present and former bindings of an item.

catchwords.doc: Describes the system used to ensure correct ordering of the quires making up an item, typically by means of annotations at the foot of the page.

collation.doc: Records a description of how the leaves or bifolia of an item are physically arranged.

colophon.doc: Contains a statement providing information regarding the date, place, agency, or reason for production of the item.

decoDesc.doc: (decoration description) Contains a description of the decoration of an item.

decoNote.doc: (decoration note) Contains a description of one or more decorative features of an item.

explicit.doc: Contains the explicit of a manuscript item; that is, the closing words of the text proper, exclusive of any rubric or colophon which might follow it.

foliation.doc: Describes the numbering system or systems used to count the leaves or pages in a codex.

heraldry.doc: Contains a heraldic formula or phrase, typically found as part of a blazon, coat of arms, etc.

layout.doc: Describes how text is laid out on the page, including information about any ruling, pricking, or other evidence of page-preparation techniques.

locus.doc: Defines a location within a manuscript or manuscript component, usually as a (possibly discontinuous) sequence of folio references.

locusGrp.doc: (locus group) Groups locations which together form a distinct but discontinuous item within a manuscript or manuscript part, according to a specific foliation.

rubric.doc: Contains a string of words through which a manuscript signals the beginning or end of a text division, often with an assertion as to its author and title, which is in some way set off from the text itself, usually in red ink, or by use of different size or type of script, or some other such visual device.

scriptDesc.doc: (script description) Contains a description of the letters or characters used in an autographic item.

scriptNote.doc: (script note) Describes a particular script distinguished within the description of an autographic item.

seal.doc: A single seal or similar attachment.

sealDesc.doc: (seal description) Describes the seals or similar external attachments applied to an item.

secFolio.doc: (second folio) Marks the word or words taken from a fixed point in a codex (typically the beginning of the second leaf) in order to provide a unique identifier for the item.

signatures.doc: Provides a description of the leaf or quire signatures found within a codex.

stamp.doc: Contains a word or phrase describing an official mark indicating ownership, genuineness, validity, etc.

support.doc: Provides a description of the physical support material of a written item.

supportDesc.doc: (support description) Groups elements describing the physical support material of an item.

typeDesc.doc: (type description) Contains a description of the typefaces or other aspects of the printing of a printed source.

typeNote.doc: (type note) Describes a particular font or other significant typographic feature of a printed resource.

addName.doc: (additional name) Contains an additional name component, such as a nickname, epithet, or alias, or any other descriptive phrase used within a personal name.

bloc.doc: Contains the name of a geopolitical unit consisting of two or more nation states or countries.

corpName.doc: (corporate name) Identifies an organization or group of people that acts as a single entity.

country.doc: Contains the name of a geopolitical unit, such as a nation, country, colony, or commonwealth, larger than or administratively superior to a region and smaller than a bloc.

district.doc: Contains the name of any kind of subdivision of a settlement, such as a parish, ward, or other administrative or geographic unit.

famName.doc: (family name) Contains a family (inherited) name, as opposed to a given, baptismal, or nick name.

foreName.doc: Contains a forename, given or baptismal name.

genName.doc: (generational name component) Contains a name component used to distinguish otherwise similar names on the basis of the relative ages or generations of the persons named.

geogFeat.doc: (geographical feature name) Contains a common noun identifying a geographical feature.

geogName.doc: (geographic name) The proper noun designation for a place, natural feature, or political jurisdiction.

nameLink.doc: (name link) Contains a connecting phrase or link used within a name but not regarded as part of it, such as "van der" or "of", "from", etc.

periodName.doc: (period name) A label that describes a period of time, such as 'Baroque' or '3rd Style period'.

persName.doc: (personal name) Designation for an individual, including any or all of that individual's forenames, surnames, honorific titles, and added names.

postBox.doc: (postal box or post office box) Contains a number or other identifier for some postal delivery point other than a street address.

postCode.doc: (postal code) Contains a numerical or alphanumeric code used as part of a postal address to simplify sorting or delivery of mail.

region.doc: Contains the name of an administrative unit such as a state, province, or county, larger than a settlement, but smaller than a country.

roleName.doc: (role name) Contains a name component which indicates that the referent has a particular role or position in society, such as an official title or rank.

settlement.doc: Contains the name of a settlement such as a city, town, or village identified as a single geopolitical or administrative unit.

street.doc: full street address including any name or number identifying a building as well as the name of the street or route on which it is located.

styleName.doc: (style name) A label for a characteristic style of writing or performance, such as 'bebop' or 'rock-n-roll'.

nc.doc: Sign representing a single pitched event, although the exact pitch may not be known.

ncGrp.doc: (neume component group) Collection of one or more neume components.

neume.doc: Sign representing one or more musical pitches.

syllable.doc: Neume notation can be thought of as "neumed text". Therefore, the syllable element provides high-level organization in this repertoire.

divLine.doc: Represents a division (divisio) in neume notation. Divisions indicate short, medium, or long pauses similar to breath marks in modern notation.

avFile.doc: (audio/video file) References an external digital audio or video file.

clip.doc: Defines a time segment of interest within a recording or within a digital audio or video file.

performance.doc: A presentation of one or more musical works.

when.doc: Indicates a point in time either absolutely (using the absolute attribute), or relative to another when element (using the since, interval and inttype attributes).

ptr.doc: (pointer) Defines a traversible pointer to another location, using only attributes to describe the destination.

ref.doc: (reference) Defines a traversible reference to another location. May contain text and sub-elements that describe the destination.

accid.doc: (accidental) Records a temporary alteration to the pitch of a note.

actor.doc: Name of an actor appearing within a cast list.

address.doc: Contains a postal address, for example of a publisher, an organization, or an individual.

addrLine.doc: (address line) Single line of a postal address.

ambitus.doc: Range of a voice, instrument or piece.

ambNote.doc: Highest or lowest pitch in a score, staff, or layer.

analytic.doc: (analytic level) Contains bibliographic elements describing an item (e.g., an article or poem) published within a monograph or journal and not as an independent publication.

annot.doc: (annotation) Provides a statement explaining the text or indicating the basis for an assertion.

arranger.doc: A person or organization who transcribes a musical composition, usually for a different medium from that of the original; in an arrangement the musical substance remains essentially unchanged.

artic.doc: (articulation) An indication of how to play a note or chord.

author.doc: The name of the creator of the intellectual content of a non-musical, literary work.

barLine.doc: Vertical line drawn through one or more staves that divides musical notation into metrical units.

bibl.doc: (bibliographic reference) Provides a loosely-structured bibliographic citation in which the sub-components may or may not be explicitly marked.

biblScope.doc: (scope of citation) Defines the scope of a bibliographic reference, for example as a list of page numbers, or a named subdivision of a larger work.

biblStruct.doc: (structured bibliographic citation) Contains a bibliographic citation in which bibliographic sub-elements must appear in a specified order.

body.doc: Contains the whole of a single musical text, excluding any front or back matter.

caesura.doc: Break, pause, or interruption in the normal tempo of a composition. Typically indicated by "railroad tracks", i.e., two diagonal slashes.

caption.doc: A label which accompanies an illustration or a table.

castGrp.doc: (cast group) Groups one or more individual castItem elements within a cast list.

castItem.doc: Contains a single entry within a cast list, describing either a single role or a list of non-speaking roles.

castList.doc: Contains a single cast list or dramatis personae.

cb.doc: (column beginning) An empty formatting element that forces text to begin in a new column.

chord.doc: A simultaneous sounding of two or more notes in the same layer *with the same duration*.

clef.doc: Indication of the exact location of a particular note on the staff and, therefore, the other notes as well.

clefGrp.doc: (clef group) A set of simultaneously-occurring clefs.

colLayout.doc: (column layout) An empty formatting element that signals the start of columnar layout.

composer.doc: The name of the creator of the intellectual content of a musical work.

contributor.doc: Names of individuals, institutions, or organizations responsible for contributions to the intellectual content of a work, where the specialized elements for authors, editors, etc. do not suffice or do not apply.

creation.doc: Non-bibliographic details of the creation of an intellectual entity, in narrative form, such as the date, place, and circumstances of its composition. More detailed information may be captured within the history element.

custos.doc: Symbol placed at the end of a line of music to indicate the first note of the next line. Sometimes called a "direct".

date.doc: A string identifying a point in time or the time period between two such points.

dedicatee.doc: Entity to whom a creative work is formally offered.

depth.doc: Description of a measurement taken through a three-dimensional object.

dimensions.doc: Information about the physical size of an entity; usually includes numerical data.

dir.doc: (directive) An instruction expressed as a combination of text and symbols, typically above, below, or between staves, but not on the staff — that is not encoded elsewhere in more specific elements, like <tempo>, <dynam> or <repeatMark>.

distributor.doc: Person or agency, other than a publisher, from which access (including electronic access) to a bibliographic entity may be obtained.

div.doc: (division) Major structural division of text, such as a preface, chapter or section.

dynam.doc: (dynamic) Indication of the volume of a note, phrase, or section of music.

edition.doc: (edition designation) A word or text phrase that indicates a difference in either content or form between the item being described and a related item previously issued by the same publisher/distributor (e.g., 2nd edition, version 2.0, etc.), or simultaneously issued by either the same publisher/distributor or another publisher/distributor (e.g., large print edition, British edition, etc.).

editor.doc: The name of the individual(s), institution(s) or organization(s) acting in an editorial capacity.

ending.doc: Alternative ending for a repeated passage of music; i.e., prima volta, seconda volta, etc.

eventList.doc: Contains historical information given as a sequence of significant past events.

expansion.doc: Indicates how a section may be programmatically expanded into its 'through-composed' form.

extent.doc: Used to express size in terms other than physical dimensions, such as number of pages, records, bytes, physical components, etc.

extData.doc: (extended data) Provides a container element for non-MEI data formats.

funder.doc: Names of individuals, institutions, or organizations responsible for funding. Funders provide financial support for a project; they are distinct from sponsors, who provide intellectual support and authority.

genre.doc: Term or terms that designate a category characterizing a particular style, form, or content.

group.doc: Contains a composite musical text, grouping together a sequence of distinct musical texts (or groups of such musical texts) which are regarded as a unit for some purpose, for example, the collected works of a composer.

grpSym.doc: (group symbol) A brace or bracket used to group two or more staves of a score or part.

head.doc: (heading) Contains any heading, for example, the title of a section of text, or the heading of a list.

height.doc: Description of the vertical size of an object.

identifier.doc: An alpha-numeric string that establishes the identity of the described material.

imprint.doc: Information relating to the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item.

incip.doc: (incipit) The opening music and/or words of a musical or textual work.

keyAccid.doc: (key accidental) Accidental in a key signature.

label.doc: A container for document text that identifies the feature to which it is attached. For a "tool tip" or other generated label, use the @label attribute.

labelAbbr.doc: A label on the pages following the first.

layer.doc: An independent stream of events on a staff.

lb.doc: (line beginning) An empty formatting element that forces text to begin on a new line.

lg.doc: (line group) May be used for any section of text that is organized as a group of lines; however, it is most often used for a group of verse lines functioning as a formal unit, e.g., a stanza, refrain, verse paragraph, etc.

librettist.doc: Person or organization who is a writer of the text of an opera, oratorio, etc.

lyricist.doc: Person or organization who is a writer of the text of a song.

mdiv.doc: (musical division) Contains a subdivision of the body of a musical text.

mei.doc: Contains a single MEI-conformant document, consisting of an MEI header and a musical text, either in isolation or as part of an meiCorpus element.

monogr.doc: (monograph level) Contains bibliographic elements describing an item, for example, a published book or journal, score, recording, or an unpublished manuscript.

music.doc: Contains a single musical text of any kind, whether unitary or composite, for example, an etude, opera, song cycle, symphony, or anthology of piano solos.

ornam.doc: An element indicating an ornament that is not a mordent, turn, or trill.

p.doc: (paragraph) One or more text phrases that form a logical prose passage.

pad.doc: (padding) An indication of extra visual space between notational elements.

part.doc: An alternative visual rendition of the score from the point of view of a particular performer (or group of performers).

parts.doc: Provides a container for performers' parts.

pb.doc: (page beginning) An empty formatting element that forces text to begin on a new page.

pgDesc.doc: (page description) Contains a brief prose description of the appearance or description of the content of a physical page.

phrase.doc: Indication of 1) a "unified melodic idea" or 2) performance technique.

physLoc.doc: (physical location) Groups information about the current physical location of a bibliographic item, such as the repository in which it is located and its shelf mark(s), and its previous locations.

publisher.doc: Name of the organization responsible for the publication of a bibliographic item.

pubPlace.doc: (publication place) Name of the place where a bibliographic item was published.

recipient.doc: The name of the individual(s), institution(s) or organization(s) receiving correspondence.

relatedItem.doc: (related item) Contains or references another bibliographic item which is related to the present one.

relation.doc: Describes a relationship or linkage amongst entities.

rend.doc: (render) A formatting element indicating special visual rendering, e.g., bold or italicized, of a text word or phrase.

repository.doc: Institution, agency, or individual which holds a bibliographic item.

resp.doc: (responsibility) A phrase describing the nature of intellectual responsibility.

respStmt.doc: (responsibility statement) Transcription of text that names one or more individuals, groups, or in rare cases, mechanical processes, responsible for creation, realization, production, funding, or distribution of the intellectual or artistic content.

rest.doc: A non-sounding event found in the source being transcribed.

role.doc: Name of a dramatic role, as given in a cast list.

roleDesc.doc: (role description) Describes a character’s role in a drama.

sb.doc: (system beginning) An empty formatting element that forces musical notation to begin on a new line.

score.doc: Full score view of the musical content.

series.doc: Contains information about the serial publication in which a bibliographic item has appeared.

space.doc: A placeholder used to fill an incomplete measure, layer, etc. most often so that the combined duration of the events equals the number of beats in the measure.

speaker.doc: Contains a specialized form of heading or label, giving the name of one or more speakers in a dramatic text or fragment.

sponsor.doc: Names of sponsoring individuals, organizations or institutions. Sponsors give their intellectual authority to a project; they are to be distinguished from funders, who provide the funding but do not necessarily take intellectual responsibility.

stack.doc: (stacked text) An inline table with a single column.

staff.doc: A group of equidistant horizontal lines on which notes are placed in order to represent pitch or a grouping element for individual 'strands' of notes, rests, etc. that may or may not actually be rendered on staff lines; that is, both diastematic and non-diastematic signs.

staffGrp.doc: (staff group) A group of bracketed or braced staves.

tempo.doc: Text and symbols descriptive of tempo, mood, or style, e.g., "allarg.", "a tempo", "cantabile", "Moderato", "♩=60", "Moderato ♩ =60").

term.doc: Keyword or phrase which describes a resource.

textLang.doc: (text language) Identifies the languages and writing systems within the work described by a bibliographic description, not the language of the description.

titlePage.doc: Contains a transcription of the title page of a text.

titlePart.doc: Contains a subsection or division of the title of a bibliographic entity.

width.doc: Description of the horizontal size of an object.

barre.doc: A barre in a chord tablature grid.

argument.doc: Contains a formal list or prose description of topics addressed.

back.doc: (back matter) Contains any appendixes, advertisements, indexes, etc. following the main body of a musical text.

epigraph.doc: Contains a quotation, anonymous or attributed, appearing on a title page.

front.doc: (front matter) Bundles prefatory text found before the start of the musical text.

imprimatur.doc: Contains a formal statement authorizing the publication of a work, sometimes required to appear on a title page or its verso.

l.doc: (line of text) Contains a single line of text within a line group.

list.doc: A formatting element that contains a series of items separated from one another and arranged in a linear, often vertical, sequence.

q.doc: (quoted) Contains material which is distinguished from the surrounding phrase-level text using quotation marks or a similar method. Use <quote> for block-level quotations.

quote.doc: (quoted material) Contains a paragraph-like block of text attributed to an external source, normally set off from the surrounding text by spacing or other typographic distinction.

seg.doc: (arbitrary segment) represents any segmentation of text below the "text component" level.

anchoredText.doc: Container for text that is fixed to a particular page location, regardless of changes made to the layout of the measures around it.

curve.doc: A curved line that cannot be represented by a more specific element, such as a slur.

mapping.doc: One or more characters which are related to the parent symbol in some respect, as specified by the type attribute.

propName.doc: (property name) Name of a property of the symbol.

symbolDef.doc: (symbol definition) Declaration of an individual symbol in a symbolTable.

symName.doc: (symbol name) Contains the name of a symbol, expressed following Unicode conventions.

symProp.doc: (symbol property) Provides a name and value for some property of the parent symbol.

symbolTable.doc: Contains a set of user-defined symbols.
